title: Dart Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: main is where this Dart program starts. print shows a value.
notes: Keep the main function around the steps.

entries.name: Keep a named number
entries.summary: var lets Dart work out a type from a value. Numbers can be added with +.
notes: A variable set to an int cannot later hold text.

entries.name: Keep a value fixed
entries.summary: final means a name can be assigned only once. It helps protect a value from accidental changes.
notes: final prevents reassignment, not every change inside a mutable object.

entries.name: Build a text message
entries.summary: A dollar sign places a variable inside a Dart string.

entries.name: Make a choice
entries.summary: if checks a Boolean rule. The else branch runs when that rule is false.
notes: A number by itself is not a Boolean condition.

entries.name: Add a list item
entries.summary: A List keeps values in order. add places a new value at the end.
notes: The first position in a List is zero.

entries.name: Visit each item
entries.summary: for-in reads each value of a list in order.
notes: The loop variable holds one item at a time.

entries.name: Return a small result
entries.summary: A function gives a calculation a name. The arrow form returns one expression.

example.code:
int twice(int n) => n * 2;
void main() { print(twice(4)); }

notes: The returned value must fit the declared type.

entries.name: Use named keys
entries.summary: A Map pairs keys and values. It can find a value by a text label.
notes: A missing map key gives null.

entries.name: Choose a fallback
entries.summary: String? can hold text or null. ?? chooses a fallback when the value is null.
notes: Using ! on null causes an error.

entries.name: Make a small object
entries.summary: A class is a plan for objects. Its constructor fills in the starting fields.
notes: Use the constructor inputs in the right order.

entries.name: Wait for a future value
entries.summary: A Future represents a result that may arrive later. await reads that result inside an async function.
notes: await belongs in an async function.
